questions.text: कुछ पुष्प एकलिंगी होते हैं, पुष्पों की एकलिंगता का अभिलक्षण किस प्रकार के परागण को अवरोधित करता है ?
questions.text_english: Some flowers are unisexual, this property of unisexuality of flowers prevents which kind of pollination ?

options.C: सजातपुष्पी परागण को परन्तु परनिषेचन को नहीं।
options.D: स्वयुग्मन को परन्तु सजातपुष्पी परागण को नहीं ।

questions.solution: Unisexual flowers (bearing either only stamens or only carpels) strictly prevent autogamy (self-pollination within the same flower) because both male and female reproductive organs are not present together in the same flower. However, if male and female unisexual flowers are present on the same plant (monoecious), geitonogamy can still occur.
questions.solution_hindi: एकलिंगी पुष्प (जिनमें केवल पुंकेसर या केवल स्त्रीकेसर होते हैं) स्वयुग्मन (उसी पुष्प के भीतर स्व-परागण) को पूरी तरह से रोकते हैं क्योंकि एक ही पुष्प में नर और मादा दोनों प्रजनन अंग मौजूद नहीं होते हैं। हालाँकि, यदि एक ही पौधे (उभयलिंगाश्रयी) पर नर और मादा एकलिंगी फूल मौजूद हैं, तो सजातपुष्पी परागण अभी भी हो सकता है।

questions.text:
पुरुषों (नर मानवों) में शुक्रजनन प्रक्रम का योजनात्मक निरूपण निम्न आरेख द्वारा दर्शाया जाता है :
उस विकल्प का चयन कीजिए जिसमें 'T', 'II', 'III' तथा 'IV' की नामांकित अवस्था को सही क्रम में दर्शाया गया है :
questions.text_english:
Given below is the schematic representation of spermatogenesis in human males:
Choose the option that shows the correct labelling of 'T', 'II', 'III' and 'IV' in the given diagram.

options.A: I: शुक्राणु, II: शुक्राणु प्रसू (शुक्राणु पूर्व), III: द्वितीयक शुक्राणु कोशिकाएँ, IV: शुक्राणुजन
options.B: I: शुक्राणुप्रसू, II: शुक्राणुजन, III: द्वितीयक शुक्राणु कोशिकाएँ, IV: शुक्राणु
options.C: I: शुक्राणुजन, II: द्वितीयक शुक्राणु कोशिकाएँ, III: शुक्राणु, IV: शुक्राणुप्रसू
options.D: I: शुक्राणुजन, II: द्वितीयक शुक्राणु कोशिकाएँ, III: शुक्राणुप्रसू, IV: शुक्राणु

options_english.A: I: spermatozoa, II: spermatid, III: sec. spermatocyte, IV: spermatogonia
options_english.B: I: spermatid, II: spermatogonia, III: sec. spermatocyte, IV: spermatozoa
options_english.C: I: spermatogonia, II: sec. spermatocyte, III: spermatozoa, IV: spermatid
options_english.D: I: spermatogonia, II: sec. spermatocyte, III: spermatid, IV: spermatozoa

questions.solution: In spermatogenesis, the process starts with diploid spermatogonia (I) at puberty. They divide mitotically to form primary spermatocytes. Primary spermatocytes undergo meiosis I to form haploid secondary spermatocytes (II). These undergo meiosis II to form haploid spermatids (III). Finally, spermatids differentiate into mature spermatozoa (IV) through spermiogenesis.
questions.solution_hindi: शुक्रजनन में, प्रक्रिया यौवन पर द्विगुणित शुक्राणुजन (spermatogonia - I) से शुरू होती है। वे समसूत्री विभाजन द्वारा प्राथमिक शुक्राणु कोशिकाएँ (primary spermatocytes) बनाते हैं। प्राथमिक शुक्राणु कोशिकाएँ अर्धसूत्री विभाजन I से गुजरकर अगुणित द्वितीयक शुक्राणु कोशिकाएँ (secondary spermatocytes - II) बनाती हैं। ये अर्धसूत्री विभाजन II से गुजरकर अगुणित शुक्राणुप्रसू (spermatids - III) बनाते हैं। अंत में, शुक्राणुप्रसू स्पर्मियोजेनेसिस के माध्यम से परिपक्व शुक्राणु (spermatozoa - IV) में विभेदित हो जाते हैं।

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा विकल्प दिए गए पौधों के विकास का सही अनुक्रम दर्शाता है ?
(i) फर्न
(ii) जिन्को
(iii) जोस्टेरोफिलम
(iv) नीटेल्स
सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
Which one of the following options shows the correct evolutionary order of the plants mentioned below ?
(i) Ferns
(ii) Ginkgo
(iii) Zosterophyllum
(iv) Gnetales
Choose the correct option.
questions.solution: Based on the evolutionary history of plants, Zosterophyllum is a primitive vascular plant ancestor. From early vascular plants evolved the Ferns. Later in evolutionary history came the gymnosperms, with Ginkgo being an older lineage followed by the more advanced Gnetales. Thus, the correct chronological order is Zosterophyllum (iii) -> Ferns (i) -> Ginkgo (ii) -> Gnetales (iv).
questions.solution_hindi: पौधों के विकासवादी इतिहास के आधार पर, जोस्टेरोफिलम (Zosterophyllum) एक आदिम संवहनी पौधे का पूर्वज है। प्रारंभिक संवहनी पौधों से फ़र्न (Ferns) विकसित हुए। विकासवादी इतिहास में बाद में अनावृतबीजी (gymnosperms) आए, जिनमें जिन्को (Ginkgo) एक पुराना वंश है जिसके बाद अधिक उन्नत नीटेल्स (Gnetales) आए। इस प्रकार, सही कालानुक्रमिक क्रम जोस्टेरोफिलम (iii) -> फ़र्न (i) -> जिन्को (ii) -> नीटेल्स (iv) है।

questions.text: 'आणविक जीव विज्ञान में आनुवंशिक सूचनाओं का प्रवाह एकदिशिक होता है।' इस सिद्धांत का प्रस्ताव करने वाले वैज्ञानिक का नाम है
questions.text_english: In molecular biology, who proposed that genetic information flows in one direction?
questions.solution: Francis Crick proposed the Central Dogma in molecular biology, which states that genetic information flows in one direction: from DNA to RNA to Protein.
questions.solution_hindi: फ्रांसिस क्रिक ने आणविक जीव विज्ञान में सेंट्रल डोग्मा (Central Dogma) का प्रस्ताव दिया, जिसमें कहा गया है कि आनुवंशिक जानकारी एक दिशा में बहती है: डीएनए से आरएनए से प्रोटीन तक।

questions.text:
सुकेन्द्रकी अनुलेखन के दौरान बनने वाले विषमांगी आरएनए को निम्न प्रकार से आरेखित किया गया है :
विषमांगी केन्द्रकीय आरएनए (hnRNA) में उपस्थित इंट्रॉनों तथा इक्ज़ॉनों की संख्या क्रमशः है :
questions.text_english:
Given below is a heterogeneous RNA formed during Eukaryotic transcription:
How many introns and exons respectively are present in the hnRNA?
questions.solution: In hnRNA, the functional coding sequences are exons (the thick segments), and the non-coding intervening sequences are introns (the thin segments). Counting them in the diagram, there are 8 thick segments (exons) and 7 thin segments (introns) alternating between them. The question asks for the number of introns and exons respectively, so it is 7 introns and 8 exons.
questions.solution_hindi: hnRNA में, कार्यात्मक कोडिंग अनुक्रम एक्सॉन (मोटे खंड) होते हैं, और गैर-कोडिंग मध्यवर्ती अनुक्रम इंट्रॉन (पतले खंड) होते हैं। आरेख में उन्हें गिनने पर, 8 मोटे खंड (एक्सॉन) और उनके बीच 7 पतले खंड (इंट्रॉन) एकांतर रूप से हैं। प्रश्न क्रमशः इंट्रॉन और एक्सॉन की संख्या पूछता है, इसलिए यह 7 इंट्रॉन और 8 एक्सॉन है।

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा अभिलक्षण मधुमक्खी (मधुप) में लिंग निर्धारण की कार्यप्रणाली को सही ढंग से अभिव्यक्त करता है ?
(i) एक शुक्राणु तथा अंडाणु के युग्मन से युग्मनज (नर) बनता है।
(ii) नर (पुंमधुप) में गुणसूत्रों की संख्या मादा मधुप के गुणसूत्रों की संख्या से आधी होती है।
(iii) मादा मधुप द्विगुणित होती है जिसमें गुणसूत्रों की संख्या 32 होती है।
(iv) नर मधुप के पिता होते हैं और वे नर संतति उत्पन्न कर सकते हैं।
सही विकल्प चुनिए :
questions.text_english:
Which of the following features correctly show the mechanism of sex-determination in honey-bees?
(i) A zygote formed from the union of a sperm and an egg develops into a male.
(ii) Males have half the number of chromosomes as that of females.
(iii) The females are diploid having 32 chromosomes.
(iv) Males have a father and can produce sons.
Choose the correct option:
questions.solution: Sex determination in honey bees is based on haplodiploidy. Females are diploid (32 chromosomes) and develop from fertilized eggs (zygotes). Males (drones) are haploid (16 chromosomes), developing parthenogenetically from unfertilized eggs, so they have half the chromosomes of females. Therefore, statements (ii) and (iii) are correct. (i) is wrong because a fertilized egg becomes a female. (iv) is wrong because males do not have a father (they come from an unfertilized egg) and cannot produce sons (they only pass genes to daughters).
questions.solution_hindi: मधुमक्खियों में लिंग निर्धारण अगुणित-द्विगुणित (haplodiploidy) पर आधारित है। मादाएं द्विगुणित (32 गुणसूत्र) होती हैं और निषेचित अंडों (युग्मनज) से विकसित होती हैं। नर (ड्रोन) अगुणित (16 गुणसूत्र) होते हैं, जो अनिषेचित अंडों से अनिषेकजनन (parthenogenetically) द्वारा विकसित होते हैं, इसलिए उनमें मादाओं की तुलना में आधे गुणसूत्र होते हैं। अतः, कथन (ii) और (iii) सही हैं। (i) गलत है क्योंकि निषेचित अंडा मादा बनता है। (iv) गलत है क्योंकि नर का कोई पिता नहीं होता है (वे अनिषेचित अंडे से आते हैं) और वे पुत्र पैदा नहीं कर सकते हैं (वे केवल बेटियों को जीन पास करते हैं)।

questions.text:
कॉलम - I तथा कॉलम-II में दी गई मदों का अध्ययन कीजिए :
कॉलम-I
(a) आरएनए पॉलीमरेज-I
(b) आरएनए पॉलीमरेज-II
(c) आरएनए पॉलीमरेज-III
कॉलम-II
(i) 18s आरआरएनए (rRNA)
(ii) एसएन आरएनएज (SnRNAs)
(iii) hn आरएनए (hnRNA)
कॉलम-I की मदों का कॉलम-II की मदों के साथ सही मिलान वाले विकल्प को चुनिए :
questions.text_english:
Study the items of Column-I and those of Column-II:
Column-I
(a) RNA polymerase I
(b) RNA polymerase II
(c) RNA polymerase III
Column-II
(i) 18s rRNA
(ii) SnRNAS
(iii) hnRNA
Choose the option that correctly matches the items of Column-I with those of Column-II:
questions.solution: In eukaryotes, there is a clear division of labor among the RNA polymerases. RNA polymerase I transcribes rRNAs (including 18S). RNA polymerase II transcribes the precursor of mRNA, which is hnRNA. RNA polymerase III is responsible for the transcription of tRNA, 5S rRNA, and snRNAs.
questions.solution_hindi: यूकेरियोट्स में, आरएनए पॉलीमरेज के बीच श्रम का स्पष्ट विभाजन है। आरएनए पॉलीमरेज I आरआरएनए (18S सहित) को अनुलेखित (transcribe) करता है। आरएनए पॉलीमरेज II एमआरएनए के पूर्ववर्ती, जो hnRNA है, को अनुलेखित करता है। आरएनए पॉलीमरेज III टीआरएनए, 5S आरआरएनए, और snRNAs के अनुलेखन के लिए जिम्मेदार है।

questions.text:
एक बच्चे का रुधिर वर्ग-A है; उसके पिता का रुधिर वर्ग-B तथा माता का रुधिर वर्ग AB है।
उस विकल्प को चुनिए जिसमें पिता, माँ (माता) तथा बच्चे के जीनप्ररूप को सही क्रम में दिया गया है :
questions.text_english:
A child with blood group A has father with blood group B and the mother with blood group AB.
Choose the option that gives the correct genotypes of father, mother and the child:
questions.solution: The child has blood group A, meaning their genotype must be either $I^AI^A$ or $I^Ai$. The mother is blood group AB, so her genotype is definitively $I^AI^B$. The father is blood group B, meaning his genotype could be $I^BI^B$ or $I^Bi$. For the child to be blood group A, they must inherit an $I^A$ allele from one parent (the mother) and either an $I^A$ or an 'i' allele from the other. Since the father is blood group B, he cannot provide an $I^A$ allele. Therefore, he must provide the 'i' allele. This means the father's genotype must be $I^Bi$ and the child's genotype must be $I^Ai$. Option C correctly lists these genotypes.
questions.solution_hindi: बच्चे का रक्त समूह A है, जिसका अर्थ है कि उसका जीनोटाइप $I^AI^A$ या $I^Ai$ होना चाहिए। माता का रक्त समूह AB है, इसलिए उसका जीनोटाइप निश्चित रूप से $I^AI^B$ है। पिता का रक्त समूह B है, जिसका अर्थ है कि उसका जीनोटाइप $I^BI^B$ या $I^Bi$ हो सकता है। बच्चे का रक्त समूह A होने के लिए, उसे एक माता-पिता (माता) से $I^A$ एलील और दूसरे से $I^A$ या 'i' एलील विरासत में मिलना चाहिए। चूँकि पिता का रक्त समूह B है, वह $I^A$ एलील प्रदान नहीं कर सकता है। इसलिए, उसे 'i' एलील प्रदान करना होगा। इसका मतलब है कि पिता का जीनोटाइप $I^Bi$ होना चाहिए और बच्चे का जीनोटाइप $I^Ai$ होना चाहिए। विकल्प C इन जीनोटाइप को सही ढंग से सूचीबद्ध करता है।

questions.text: मानव रुधिर में टी-लसीकाणुओं की संख्या के ह्रास होने के परिणामस्वरूप होता है
questions.text_english: The decrease in the T-Lymphocytes count in human blood will finally result in
questions.solution: T-lymphocytes (helper T-cells) play a crucial role in the immune system by stimulating B-lymphocytes to produce antibodies. A significant decrease in the T-lymphocyte count (as seen in HIV infection) impairs the activation of B-cells, leading to a decrease in the production of antibodies.
questions.solution_hindi: टी-लिम्फोसाइट्स (हेल्पर टी-सेल) बी-लिम्फोसाइट्स को एंटीबॉडी (प्रतिरक्षी) का उत्पादन करने के लिए उत्तेजित करके प्रतिरक्षा प्रणाली में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाते हैं। टी-लिम्फोसाइट की संख्या में महत्वपूर्ण कमी (जैसे कि एचआईवी संक्रमण में देखा गया है) बी-कोशिकाओं की सक्रियता को बाधित करती है, जिससे एंटीबॉडी के उत्पादन में कमी आती है।

questions.text: यदि मेसेल्सन तथा स्टाल के प्रयोग को 80 मिनट तक (तीसरी पीढ़ी) जारी रखा जाए तो संवर्धन में $N^{15}/N^{15}$: N15/N14: N14/N14 युक्त डीएनए का अनुपात क्या होगा ?
questions.text_english: If Meselson and Stahl's experiment is continued for 80 minutes (till III generation) then what would be the ratio of DNA containing $N^{15}/N^{15}$: $N^{15}/N^{14}$: $N^{14}/N^{14}$ in the medium ?
questions.solution: E. coli divides every 20 minutes. Initially (0 min), all DNA is heavy ($N^{15}/N^{15}$). After 20 mins (1st generation), all DNA is hybrid ($N^{15}/N^{14}$). After 40 mins (2nd generation), the ratio of hybrid to light ($N^{14}/N^{14}$) is 1:1. After 60 mins (3rd generation), there are 2 hybrid and 6 light DNA molecules, ratio 1:3. After 80 mins (4th generation), there are 2 hybrid and 14 light DNA molecules, ratio 1:7. The question states "till III generation" but asks for 80 minutes. The standard Meselson-Stahl experiment defines generation time as 20 mins. 80 mins is 4 generations. However, 80 mins is often presented in a simplified context where 0-20 is 1st, 20-40 is 2nd, 40-60 is 3rd, and 60-80 is 4th. Re-reading the question, it asks for the ratio of $N^{15}/N^{15}$: $N^{15}/N^{14}$: $N^{14}/N^{14}$. Heavy DNA ($N^{15}/N^{15}$) is 0. The number of hybrid molecules always remains 2. Total DNA molecules after 3 generations (60 mins) is $2^3 = 8$. So, 2 hybrid, 6 light. Ratio is 0:2:6 -> 0:1:3. If it means 80 minutes (4 generations), total is 16. 2 hybrid, 14 light. Ratio 0:2:14 -> 0:1:7. Let's assume the question meant 60 minutes for the 3rd generation, which gives 0:1:3. The options provide 0:1:3, which fits the 3rd generation (60 mins) perfectly.

sub_questions.text_english: (A) Comment upon the mode of pollination in Vallisneria and Zostera.

key_points: Vallisneria: Pollination occurs on the surface of water (Epihydrophily). The female flower reaches the surface by a long stalk and male flowers/pollen grains are released on the water surface and carried passively by water currents.

Zostera (sea grasses): Pollination occurs beneath the surface of water (Hypohydrophily). Female flowers remain submerged and long, ribbon-like pollen grains are released inside the water and carried passively by water currents.

sub_questions.solution: Both Vallisneria and Zostera are aquatic plants that use water as the pollinating agent (hydrophily). However, their mechanisms differ. In Vallisneria, the female flower reaches the water surface via a long stalk. Male flowers or pollen grains are released onto the surface of the water. They are carried passively by water currents, and some eventually reach the female flowers and the stigma. This is an example of epihydrophily. In Zostera (marine sea grasses), female flowers remain submerged in water. The pollen grains are long, ribbon-like, and are released inside the water. They are carried passively by water currents to reach the stigma. This is an example of hypohydrophily.

sub_questions.text: (B) पुष्पी पादपों द्वारा स्वपरागण को हतोत्साहित करने हेतु अपनाई गई चार कार्यप्रणालियों का उल्लेख कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: (B) Mention any four strategies adopted by flowering plants to prevent self-pollination.

key_points: Dichogamy: Pollen release and stigma receptivity are not synchronised (e.g., protandry or protogyny).
Herkogamy: Anther and stigma are placed at different positions so that pollen cannot come in contact with the stigma of the same flower.
Self-incompatibility: A genetic mechanism that prevents self-pollen from fertilizing the ovules by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen tube growth in the pistil.

Production of unisexual flowers: If both male and female flowers are present on the same plant (monoecious), it prevents autogamy but not geitonogamy. If present on different plants (dioecious), it prevents both.

sub_questions.solution: Flowering plants have developed several outbreeding devices to discourage self-pollination and encourage cross-pollination. Four major strategies are: 1. Pollen release and stigma receptivity are not synchronized (dichogamy); either the pollen is released before the stigma becomes receptive or vice versa. 2. The anther and stigma are placed at different positions (herkogamy) so that pollen cannot easily reach the stigma of the same flower. 3. Self-incompatibility, which is a genetic mechanism preventing self-pollen from fertilizing the ovules by inhibiting pollen germination or tube growth. 4. Production of unisexual flowers, which completely prevents autogamy, and if the plant is dioecious, it prevents geitonogamy as well.

questions.solution: The student must choose one of two options. Option A requires knowledge of specific hydrophilous pollination mechanisms in Vallisneria and Zostera. Option B requires listing four outbreeding devices in flowering plants.

sub_questions.text: (A) ऐसी किन्हीं दो परिस्थितियों का वर्णन कीजिए जिसमें एक चिकित्सक (डॉक्टर) पूर्वनिर्मित प्रतिरक्षियों (प्रतिआविष) को रोगी व्यक्ति के शरीर में निवेशित करने की सलाह देते हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: (A) Describe any two situations where a medical doctor would recommend injection of a pre-formed antibodies (antitoxins) into the body of a patient.

key_points: Situation 1: Tetanus infection - When a person is infected with deadly bacteria like tetanus, they require a quick, immediate immune response, which is achieved by injecting preformed antibodies or antitoxins.
Situation 2: Snakebite - In cases of snakebites, the injection contains preformed antibodies against the snake venom to rapidly neutralize the lethal toxins.

sub_questions.solution: A medical doctor recommends the injection of pre-formed antibodies (a process creating artificial passive immunity) in situations where an extremely rapid immune response is required to save the patient's life, and the body does not have enough time to naturally produce its own antibodies. Two primary examples are: 1. When a person is suspected of being infected with tetanus (e.g., from a deep puncture wound), an injection containing preformed antibodies or antitoxins is administered immediately. 2. When a person is bitten by a venomous snake, the antivenom injection given contains preformed antibodies specifically designed to neutralize the fast-acting snake venom.

sub_questions.text: (B) संक्रमित मादा ऐनोफेलीज़ मच्छर के काटने के परिणामस्वरूप मलेरिया रोग के बीजाणुजों (स्पोरोजॉइट्स) के मानव शरीर में प्रविष्ट होने के तुरंत बाद मलेरिया के अभिलक्षण परिलक्षित नहीं होते हैं। व्याख्या कीजिए कि ऐसा क्यों होता है।
sub_questions.text_english: (B) The symptoms of malaria do not appear immediately after the entry of sporozoites into the human body when bitten by female Anopheles mosquito. Explain why it happens.

key_points: The sporozoites first travel through the blood to the liver, where they multiply asexually inside the liver cells.
After multiplying in the liver, they burst the liver cells and are released into the blood, where they attack and enter the red blood cells (RBCs).
Inside the RBCs, they multiply asexually again and cause the RBCs to rupture.
The rupture of RBCs is associated with the release of a toxic substance, haemozoin, which is responsible for the symptoms (chill and high fever). Symptoms only appear after this sequence of events.

sub_questions.solution: Symptoms of malaria do not appear immediately upon infection because the parasite goes through an incubation period involving complex multiplication stages before producing toxins. When sporozoites enter the human body, they initially travel to the liver and multiply asexually within the liver cells. This multiplication eventually causes the liver cells to burst, releasing the parasites back into the bloodstream. The parasites then attack the red blood cells (RBCs), where they multiply asexually again. Only when these infected RBCs rupture do they release a toxic substance called haemozoin into the bloodstream. The release of haemozoin is what triggers the characteristic symptoms of malaria, such as chills and high fever recurring every 3-4 days. This entire multiplication process takes time, hence the delay in symptom onset.

sub_questions.text_english: (a) List two reasons that make copper releasing IUDs as effective contraceptives.

key_points: IUDs increase the phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus.
The Copper ions (Cu++) released strongly suppress sperm motility and severely impair the fertilizing capacity of the sperms.

sub_questions.solution: Copper-releasing IUDs (Intra Uterine Devices), such as CuT or Multiload 375, are highly effective contraceptives due to two primary mechanisms. Firstly, the physical presence of the device in the uterus induces an inflammatory response that increases the phagocytosis (cellular engulfment and destruction) of sperms. Secondly, the continual release of copper ions (Cu++) creates a toxic environment that heavily suppresses sperm motility (swimming ability) and significantly reduces their capacity to successfully fertilize an ovum.

sub_questions.text_english: (b) Explain how the intake of oral contraceptive pills prevent pregnancy in humans.

key_points: They primarily inhibit ovulation (release of the egg from the ovary) due to the presence of progestogens or progestogen-estrogen combinations.
They inhibit implantation by altering the uterine endometrium, making it unsuitable.
They alter the quality of cervical mucus to prevent or severely retard the entry of sperms.

sub_questions.solution: Oral contraceptive pills prevent pregnancy through a multi-faceted hormonal approach. These pills, containing progestogens or a combination of progestogen and estrogen, exert negative feedback on the pituitary gland, preventing the surge of Luteinizing Hormone (LH) and thus primarily inhibiting ovulation. Without an egg released, fertilization cannot occur. Additionally, the hormones alter the endometrium lining of the uterus, making it unsuitable for implantation even if fertilization somehow happened. Finally, they cause the cervical mucus to become thick and sticky, creating a physical barrier that prevents or retards the entry of sperms into the uterus.

questions.text_english:
(a) A bilobed dithecous anther has 200 microspore mother cells per microsporangium. How many male gametophytes can be produced by this anther?
(b) Write the composition of intine and exine layers of a pollen grains.

sub_questions.text: (a) एक द्विकोष्ठी परागकोश की प्रत्येक लघुबीजाणुधानी में 200 लघुबीजाणु मातृ कोशिकाएँ हैं। इस परागकोश से कितने नरयुग्मकोद्भिद् उत्पन्न (निर्मित) होंगे ?
sub_questions.text_english: (a) A bilobed dithecous anther has 200 microspore mother cells per microsporangium. How many male gametophytes can be produced by this anther?

key_points: A typical bilobed dithecous anther consists of 4 microsporangia.
Total microspore mother cells (MMCs) = 4 microsporangia * 200 MMCs/microsporangium = 800 MMCs.
Each MMC undergoes meiosis to produce 4 microspores (which develop into male gametophytes/pollen grains).
Total male gametophytes = 800 MMCs * 4 = 3200.

sub_questions.solution: A bilobed dithecous anther contains four microsporangia (pollen sacs). If there are 200 microspore mother cells (MMCs) per microsporangium, the total number of MMCs in the entire anther is 4 multiplied by 200, which equals 800 MMCs. During microsporogenesis, each diploid MMC undergoes meiosis to produce a tetrad of four haploid microspores, and each microspore develops into a male gametophyte (pollen grain). Therefore, the total number of male gametophytes produced by the anther is 800 MMCs multiplied by 4, resulting in 3200 male gametophytes.

sub_questions.text: (b) एक परागकण के बाह्य चोल तथा अंतःचोल परतों के संगठन (संरचना) का वर्णन कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Write the composition of intine and exine layers of a pollen grains.

key_points: Exine composition: It is the hard outer layer made up of sporopollenin.
Intine composition: It is the thin, continuous inner layer made up of cellulose and pectin.

sub_questions.solution: A mature pollen grain has a two-layered wall. The prominent outer layer is the exine. It is exceptionally hard and highly resistant, composed primarily of sporopollenin, one of the most resistant organic materials known, which can withstand high temperatures and strong acids or alkalis. The inner layer is the intine. In contrast to the exine, the intine is a thin, continuous membrane. It is chemically composed of cellulose and pectin.

questions.text: प्राकृतिक वरण हार्डी-विनबर्ग संतुलन को किस प्रकार प्रभावित करता है ? ग्राफ की सहायता से इसकी व्याख्या कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: How does the process of Natural Selection affect Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium? Explain with the help of graphs.

key_points: State that Natural Selection alters allele frequencies, thus disrupting the Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium.
Describe Stabilising Selection: More individuals acquire mean character value. Draw a graph showing the peak gets higher and narrower.
Describe Directional Selection: More individuals acquire value other than the mean character value. Draw a graph showing the peak shifts in one direction.
Describe Disruptive Selection: More individuals acquire peripheral character values at both ends of the distribution curve. Draw a graph showing two peaks forming.

questions.solution:
The Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium states that allele frequencies in a population will remain constant from generation to generation in the absence of evolutionary influences. Natural selection is a primary force that disrupts this equilibrium by differentially favoring the survival and reproduction of certain phenotypes over others, thereby changing allele frequencies. Natural selection can affect traits in three main ways, represented graphically:
1. Stabilising Selection: The environment favors intermediate phenotypes and acts against extreme variants. Graphically, the original bell-shaped curve becomes narrower and the central peak becomes higher, indicating that more individuals acquire the mean character value.
2. Directional Selection: The environment favors phenotypes at one extreme of the existing variation range. Graphically, the entire bell curve shifts in the direction of the favored extreme, moving the peak towards one side as more individuals acquire a character value other than the original mean.
3. Disruptive Selection: The environment favors both extreme phenotypes simultaneously while acting against the intermediate phenotypes. Graphically, the center of the curve dips while the two peripheral ends rise, eventually forming a curve with two distinct peaks.
questions.solution_hindi:
हार्डी-वेनबर्ग संतुलन बताता है कि विकासवादी प्रभावों की अनुपस्थिति में एक आबादी में एलील आवृत्तियां पीढ़ी दर पीढ़ी स्थिर रहेंगी। प्राकृतिक वरण (Natural selection) कुछ फीनोटाइप के अस्तित्व और प्रजनन का पक्ष लेकर इस संतुलन को बाधित करता है, जिससे एलील आवृत्तियां बदल जाती हैं। प्राकृतिक वरण तीन मुख्य तरीकों से काम कर सकता है:
1. स्थायीकारक (Stabilising): प्रकृति औसत या मध्यवर्ती लक्षणों का पक्ष लेती है। ग्राफ में, शिखर ऊँचा और संकरा हो जाता है क्योंकि अधिक व्यक्ति औसत लक्षण मान प्राप्त करते हैं।
2. दिशिक (Directional): प्रकृति एक चरम लक्षण का पक्ष लेती है। ग्राफ में, शिखर एक दिशा में खिसक जाता है क्योंकि अधिक व्यक्ति औसत लक्षण मान के अलावा अन्य मान प्राप्त करते हैं।
3. विदारी (Disruptive): प्रकृति दोनों चरम लक्षणों का पक्ष लेती है और मध्यवर्ती को अस्वीकार करती है। ग्राफ में, दो शिखर बनते हैं क्योंकि अधिक व्यक्ति वितरण वक्र के दोनों सिरों पर परिधीय लक्षण मान प्राप्त करते हैं।

questions.text_english: Using a Punnett square workout the distribution of an autosomal phenotypic feature in the first filial generation after a cross between a homozygous female and a heterozygous male for a single locus.

key_points: Identify the genotypes of the parents. Let the alleles be A (dominant) and a (recessive). The heterozygous male is Aa. The homozygous female can be either homozygous dominant (AA) or homozygous recessive (aa). Both cases must be shown or one clearly assumed.
Case 1 (Female AA x Male Aa): Draw a Punnett square with gametes A, A from female and A, a from male. Offspring genotypes: 50% AA, 50% Aa. Phenotypic distribution: 100% dominant phenotype.

Case 2 (Female aa x Male Aa): Draw a Punnett square with gametes a, a from female and A, a from male. Offspring genotypes: 50% Aa, 50% aa. Phenotypic distribution: 50% dominant phenotype, 50% recessive phenotype.

questions.solution:
To determine the distribution of an autosomal phenotypic feature for a single locus, let's denote the dominant allele as 'A' and the recessive allele as 'a'. The male is explicitly stated to be heterozygous, so his genotype is 'Aa', producing gametes 'A' and 'a'. The female is homozygous, which means she could be either homozygous dominant (AA) or homozygous recessive (aa). 

Scenario 1: Female is homozygous recessive (aa) crossed with heterozygous male (Aa). This is effectively a test cross.
- Female gametes: a, a
- Male gametes: A, a
Punnett Square:
| | a | a |
|---|---|---|
| A | Aa | Aa |
| a | aa | aa |
Genotypic ratio: 1 Aa : 1 aa (50% heterozygous, 50% homozygous recessive).
Phenotypic ratio: 1 Dominant : 1 Recessive (50% dominant feature, 50% recessive feature).

Scenario 2: Female is homozygous dominant (AA) crossed with heterozygous male (Aa).
- Female gametes: A, A
- Male gametes: A, a
Punnett Square:
| | A | A |
|---|---|---|
| A | AA | AA |
| a | Aa | Aa |
Genotypic ratio: 1 AA : 1 Aa (50% homozygous dominant, 50% heterozygous).
Phenotypic ratio: All offspring (100%) will display the dominant phenotypic feature.

questions.text_english:
An application of biotechnology in agriculture involves the production of pest resistant plants, using "cry" gene from a bacterium, Bacillus thuringiensis.
(a) Proteins coded by which specific Bt. toxin gene control corn borer?
(b) How does Bt. toxin produced by the bacterium kill the insect? Explain.

sub_questions.text: (a) किस विशिष्ट बीटी. जीवविष जीन द्वारा कूटलेखित प्रोटीन मक्का वेधक (बोरर) का नियंत्रण करते हैं ?
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Proteins coded by which specific Bt. toxin gene control corn borer?

key_points: The specific gene is cryIAb.

sub_questions.solution: The toxic proteins that specifically target and control the corn borer insect pest are coded by the specific Bt toxin gene named cryIAb.

sub_questions.text: (b) जीवाणु द्वारा निर्मित बीटी. जीवविष कीट को किस प्रकार मारता है ? व्याख्या कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) How does Bt. toxin produced by the bacterium kill the insect? Explain.

key_points: Bt toxin is produced by the bacterium as an inactive crystal protein (protoxin).
When an insect ingests the inactive toxin, it reaches the midgut. The highly alkaline pH of the insect's gut solubilizes the crystals, converting the inactive protoxin into an active toxic form.
The activated toxin heavily binds to the surface receptors on the midgut epithelial cells, creating pores.
These pores cause severe cell swelling and lysis (bursting), eventually leading to the death of the insect.

sub_questions.solution: Bacillus thuringiensis produces the Bt toxin in an inactive, crystalline form known as a protoxin, which is why it does not kill the bacterium itself. However, when a susceptible insect ingests this inactive toxin by eating the transgenic plant tissue, it enters the insect's midgut. The highly alkaline pH environment of the insect's gut solubilizes the protein crystals, instantly converting the inactive protoxin into an active toxin. This newly activated toxin then binds specifically to receptor sites on the surface of the midgut epithelial cells. This binding creates large pores in the cell membranes, which disrupts osmotic balance, causing the epithelial cells to swell enormously and eventually lyse (burst). The extensive damage to the midgut lining leads to starvation and the subsequent death of the insect.

questions.solution: This question tests knowledge of the biotechnological application of Bt toxin in agriculture. It specifically targets the identification of the gene responsible for corn borer resistance and requires a detailed explanation of the biochemical mechanism by which the Bt protoxin becomes lethal inside the insect's digestive tract.

(d) How is active immunity different from passive immunity?

key_points: Source of antibodies: In active immunity, antibodies are actively produced by the host's own body in response to exposure to antigens. In passive immunity, ready-made, pre-formed antibodies are directly injected from an external source.
Response time: Active immunity is a slow process taking considerable time to fully develop an effective response. Passive immunity instantly provides an immediate, fast-acting protective shield.
Memory: Active immunity generates immunological memory for long-term protection. Passive immunity provides no memory and is strictly temporary.

sub_questions.solution: Active immunity fundamentally differs from passive immunity in several key ways. Firstly, regarding the source of antibodies: in active immunity, the host's own immune system is actively stimulated by antigens (like an infection or vaccine) to synthesize its own protective antibodies. In passive immunity, pre-formed, ready-made antibodies generated externally (like in a horse or from a mother's milk) are directly transferred into the host. Secondly, regarding response time: active immunity is a relatively slow biological process that takes time to build up a robust defense, while passive immunity provides an immediate, fast-acting response. Lastly, active immunity provides long-lasting protection by generating memory cells, whereas passive immunity provides only temporary protection as the injected antibodies degrade over time and no memory is established.

key_points: (i) Schematic representation must show Oogonia multiplying by mitosis to form Primary Oocytes. Primary Oocytes undergo Meiosis I (arrested at prophase I) to yield a large Secondary Oocyte and a tiny first polar body. The Secondary Oocyte undergoes Meiosis II (completed only if fertilization occurs) to yield the Ovum and a second polar body.
(ii) Chromosome numbers: Oogonia = 46. Primary Oocyte = 46. Secondary Oocyte = 23. First polar body = 23. Ovum = 23. Second polar body = 23.

(ii) Correlation with life phases: Oogonia multiplication and formation of primary oocytes occurs strictly during fetal life (before birth). The completion of Meiosis I and release of the secondary oocyte occurs cyclically starting from puberty (during reproductive adult life). Completion of Meiosis II occurs only upon fertilization by a sperm.

sub_questions.solution: Oogenesis is a complex, discontinuous process. The schematic representation begins with diploid Oogonia (46 chromosomes). These multiply via mitosis to form primary oocytes (46 chromosomes). This initial phase occurs entirely during embryonic development, meaning no new oogonia are formed after birth. The primary oocytes start Meiosis I but are arrested in prophase I. Years later, starting at puberty and continuing cyclically, a primary oocyte completes Meiosis I to form a massive haploid secondary oocyte (23 chromosomes) and a tiny, non-functional first polar body (23 chromosomes). This secondary oocyte is released during ovulation. The secondary oocyte then begins Meiosis II but is arrested at metaphase II. It only completes Meiosis II if a sperm successfully penetrates it, leading to the formation of the mature haploid ovum (23 chromosomes) and a second polar body.

key_points: (i) Autogamy: Pollen grains are transferred from the anther to the stigma of the exact same flower. This leads to inbreeding.

(i) Geitonogamy: Pollen grains are transferred from the anther of one flower to the stigma of another different flower located on the exact same plant. Genetically similar to autogamy but ecologically requires a pollinator.
(i) Xenogamy: Pollen grains are transferred from the anther of a flower on one plant to the stigma of a flower on an entirely different plant of the same species. This ensures genetic variation.

sub_questions.solution:
In chasmogamous (open) bisexual flowers, three modes of pollination are possible based on the source of pollen. 1. Autogamy: This is self-pollination where pollen from the anther lands on the stigma of the very same flower. 2. Geitonogamy: This involves the transfer of pollen from the anther of one flower to the stigma of another flower residing on the same individual plant. It requires a pollinator but is genetically similar to autogamy. 3. Xenogamy: This is true cross-pollination, where pollen from an anther is carried to the stigma of a flower on a different plant of the same species, bringing genetic variation.

sub_questions.text_english:
(A) (i) Explain how is a bacterial cell made 'competent to take up recombinant DNA from the medium.
(ii) Explain the steps of amplification of gene of interest using PCR technique.

key_points: (i) Competency treatment: DNA is hydrophilic and cannot pass cell membranes naturally. Bacterial cells are treated with a specific concentration of a divalent cation (like calcium), which increases the efficiency of DNA entry through pores in its cell wall.

(i) Heat shock: The treated cells are incubated with recombinant DNA on ice, then briefly subjected to a heat shock at 42°C, and then put back on ice. This forces the bacteria to take up the recombinant DNA.
(ii) PCR Step 1 - Denaturation: The double-stranded DNA is heated to a high temperature (approx 94°C) to break hydrogen bonds, creating two single DNA strands.

(ii) PCR Step 2 - Annealing: The temperature is lowered, allowing two sets of chemically synthesized oligonucleotide primers to bind to complementary regions at the 3' ends of the separated DNA strands.

(ii) PCR Step 3 - Extension/Elongation: The thermostable enzyme Taq DNA polymerase uses free nucleotides to extend the primers, synthesizing new DNA strands complementary to the templates, thereby amplifying the target gene.

sub_questions.solution:
Because DNA is a hydrophilic molecule, it cannot simply diffuse through the hydrophobic lipid bilayer of a bacterial cell membrane. To force bacteria to take up recombinant DNA, they must be made 'competent'. This is achieved by first soaking the bacterial cells in a cold solution containing a specific concentration of a divalent cation, typically calcium chloride. This chemical treatment alters the cell wall, making it more permeable. Following this, the cells undergo a physical 'heat shock'. The competent cells and recombinant plasmids are mixed on ice, then rapidly transferred to a water bath at 42°C for a very brief period, and immediately plunged back onto ice. This drastic temperature shift creates a transient pressure difference that physically forces the recombinant DNA directly through the enlarged pores into the bacterium.
To amplify a gene of interest using Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR), a machine cycles through three distinct temperature steps. 
1. Denaturation: The reaction mixture containing the target DNA is heated to a very high temperature (around 94°C). The intense thermal energy breaks the weak hydrogen bonds holding the double helix together, resulting in two separate, single-stranded DNA templates.
2. Annealing: The temperature is quickly lowered (around 50-65°C). This cooler environment allows two sets of short, chemically synthesized RNA or DNA primers to specifically bind (anneal) to their complementary target sequences flanking the gene of interest on the 3' ends of both separated strands.
3. Extension: The temperature is raised slightly to the optimal working temperature (around 72°C) of a specialized, heat-resistant enzyme called Taq DNA polymerase. This robust enzyme reads the template strands and rapidly adds free deoxynucleotides extending from the primers, synthesizing entirely new complementary DNA strands. Repeating these three steps 30 times can amplify a single DNA segment a billion-fold.

key_points: (i) Definition: Transgenic animals are those whose original DNA has been deliberately manipulated by humans to possess and express an extra, foreign gene.
(ii) Reason 1: Study of Normal Physiology and Development - They are specifically designed to study how genes are regulated and how they deeply affect normal bodily functions and complex development.

(ii) Reason 2: Study of Disease - They serve as invaluable biological models for complex human diseases (like cancer, cystic fibrosis, rheumatoid arthritis) facilitating deep investigation into disease progression and new therapeutic treatments.

(ii) Reason 3: Biological Products - They are genetically modified to act as living bioreactors, producing highly valuable human medical proteins directly into their milk or blood, such as alpha-1-antitrypsin used to treat severe emphysema.

(ii) Reason 4: Vaccine Safety Testing - Transgenic mice are heavily utilized to test the safety and efficacy of newly developed vaccines (like the polio vaccine) before they are ever administered to humans.

sub_questions.solution:
Transgenic animals are biologically engineered organisms whose original genome has been deliberately manipulated by scientists using recombinant DNA technology to permanently insert and express an extra, foreign gene (a transgene) from another species. 
These genetically modified animals are produced for several highly beneficial reasons serving humanity and science: 
1. Study of normal physiology and development: Scientists engineer these animals to study exactly how specific genes are naturally regulated, how they interact, and how they profoundly affect the normal functions and development of the body.
2. Study of disease: Transgenic animals, especially mice, act as critical biological models for human diseases. They are engineered to carry the genes responsible for human ailments like cancer, cystic fibrosis, and Alzheimer's, allowing researchers to study disease progression and aggressively test novel drugs and therapies.
3. Biological products: Certain transgenic animals are transformed into biological factories. For example, transgenic cows or sheep are designed to produce highly valuable and otherwise expensive human therapeutic proteins (like alpha-1-antitrypsin for emphysema) directly into their milk, making harvesting very efficient.
4. Vaccine safety testing: Before any new vaccine is approved for human use, it must undergo rigorous safety testing. Transgenic mice, engineered to react similarly to humans, are heavily utilized to test the safety and efficacy of newly developed vaccines, such as the polio vaccine, ensuring human safety.

(A) (i) Explain giving three reasons why tropics show greatest levels of species diversity.
(ii) Draw a graph showing species-area relationship. Name the naturalist who studied such relationship. Write the observation made by him.

key_points: (i) Reason 1 (Evolutionary time): Unlike temperate regions subjected to frequent glaciations in the past, tropical latitudes have remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years, providing a long evolutionary time for species diversification.

(i) Reason 2 (Environmental stability): Tropical environments are less seasonal, relatively more constant, and highly predictable. Such stable environments promote niche specialization and lead to greater species diversity.

(i) Reason 3 (Solar energy): There is substantially more solar energy available in the tropics, which directly contributes to higher biological productivity; higher productivity invariably supports greater overall diversity.
(ii) Draw graph: Plot 'Area' on the x-axis and 'Species Richness' on the y-axis, drawing a rectangular hyperbola curve ($S=CA^z$).
(ii) Naturalist: Alexander von Humboldt.
(ii) Observation: He observed that within a region, species richness increased with increasing explored area, but only up to a limit.

sub_questions.solution:
Tropical environments consistently exhibit the highest levels of species biodiversity across the globe for three primary ecological reasons. First, evolutionary time: while temperate regions were repeatedly devastated by frequent glaciations (ice ages) over geological history, tropical latitudes have remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years. This long, stable period provided ample evolutionary time for complex species diversification to occur unhindered. Second, environmental stability: tropical climates are much less seasonal, and generally more constant and highly predictable compared to erratic temperate climates. This constant stability promotes intense niche specialization, allowing a greater number of species to coexist. Third, higher solar energy: the tropics receive significantly more direct solar radiation year-round. This abundant energy fuels massive primary productivity in plants, and this high productivity base is able to support and sustain a much larger and more diverse food web.
Regarding the species-area relationship, the graph must plot 'Area' on the x-axis and 'Species Richness' on the y-axis, displaying a classic curve that rises sharply and then levels off, known mathematically as a rectangular hyperbola ($S=CA^z$). This fundamental ecological relationship was extensively studied by the great German naturalist and geographer Alexander von Humboldt. During his pioneering explorations in South American jungles, he meticulously observed and formally concluded that within any given region, species richness steadily increases as the area of explored territory increases, but crucially, this increase only occurs up to a certain limit, after which it plateaus.

(B) (i) The world is facing the accelerated rate of species extinctions due to human activities. Explain any three major causes of biodiversity losses.
(ii) Describe 'Ex situ' approach for conserving biodiversity. Give any two examples.

key_points: (i) Cause 1: Habitat loss and fragmentation. This is the most important cause driving animals and plants to extinction, usually due to human clearing of forests for agriculture or urban development, breaking large habitats into small fragments.

(i) Cause 2: Over-exploitation. When human 'need' turns to 'greed', it leads to the relentless over-harvesting of natural resources, pushing species like the Steller's sea cow and passenger pigeon to extinction.

(i) Cause 3: Alien species invasions. When alien (non-native) species are introduced unintentionally or deliberately into a new habitat, some turn highly invasive and fiercely outcompete or prey upon indigenous species, causing their decline or extinction (e.g., Nile perch introduced into Lake Victoria).

(ii) Ex situ conservation: This approach involves deliberately taking threatened or endangered animals and plants completely out of their natural habitats and placing them in highly protected, artificial settings where they can be given specialized care and bred.
(ii) Examples: Zoological parks, botanical gardens, wildlife safari parks, seed banks, or cryopreservation facilities.

sub_questions.solution:
The catastrophic loss of global biodiversity is primarily driven by human activities, categorized into the 'Evil Quartet'. Three major causes are: 
1. Habitat loss and fragmentation: This is arguably the most severe threat. As massive tracts of natural ecosystems, especially tropical rainforests, are aggressively cleared for agricultural expansion or urban development, indigenous species lose their homes. Furthermore, when large habitats are broken into small fragments by roads or settlements, mammals and birds requiring large territories suffer drastically and populations crash.
2. Over-exploitation: Humans have always depended on nature for food and shelter, but when necessity escalates to unrestrained greed, massive over-exploitation occurs. Many marine fish populations worldwide are currently overharvested, endangering their continued existence, similar to historical extinctions like the passenger pigeon.
3. Alien species invasions: When foreign, non-native species are introduced into a new ecosystem, either by accident or design, some establish themselves aggressively. Lacking natural predators in the new environment, they become highly invasive, fiercely outcompeting or directly predating upon fragile indigenous species, driving them towards extinction (e.g., the introduction of the Nile perch decimated native cichlid fish in Lake Victoria).
To combat these losses, conservationists employ the 'Ex situ' (off-site) conservation approach. In this highly managed strategy, critically threatened or endangered animals and plants are physically removed from their failing natural habitats. They are then relocated into specialized, artificial, and fully protected environments where experts can provide dedicated care, feeding, and breeding programs to ensure their survival and prevent absolute extinction. Prime examples of ex situ conservation facilities include expansive zoological parks, highly curated botanical gardens, wildlife safari parks, and advanced cryopreservation seed banks.
